# tenzro-node reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-api-docs.py from crates/tenzro-node/src/main.rs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every flag and subcommand of the `tenzro-node` binary, from its own argument definitions. Run `tenzro-node --help` for the same text on your build. The CLI (`tenzro`) is in [CLI.md](CLI.md); how to deploy a node is in [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md).

## Flags

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` / `-c` | `FILE` |  |  | Path to configuration file |
| `--data-dir` / `-d` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | Data directory. Also settable via `$TENZRO_DATA_DIR` so an operator can pin it once — in the environment, a service unit, a shell profile — rather than repeating the flag on every start; the flag wins when both are given. |
| `--tpm-key-holder` | `SOCKET` | `TENZRO_TPM_KEY_HOLDER` |  | Hold this machine's identity key in another machine's TPM instead of a local one, through the key holder listening on this socket (`tenzro-node tpm key-holder`). The holder keeps this boot's transport key in memory and the operator passkey's grant for it. |
| `--tpm-label` | `LABEL` | `TENZRO_TPM_LABEL` |  | The key label the provider enrolled for this machine. |
| `--reserve-gb` | `GB` | `TENZRO_RESERVE_GB` |  | GiB held back from models for the OS, this process, RocksDB, iroh, and the service surfaces — never lent to a model at any load. Defaults to 16. Also settable via `$TENZRO_RESERVE_GB`; the flag wins when both are given. Lower it on a node that only serves models; raise it on one carrying a deep RocksDB working set or co-hosting other services. |
| `--resident-ceiling-gb` | `GB` | `TENZRO_RESIDENT_CEILING_GB` |  | GiB ceiling for always-resident models (language models, embeddings, forecasting, ASR, TTS). Omit to use 60% of what remains after the reserve. Also settable via `$TENZRO_RESIDENT_CEILING_GB`; the flag wins when both are given. |
| `--on-demand-ceiling-gb` | `GB` | `TENZRO_ON_DEMAND_CEILING_GB` |  | GiB ceiling for pipelines loaded per job and evicted afterwards — image and video generation. Omit to use whatever the resident tier does not take. Also settable via `$TENZRO_ON_DEMAND_CEILING_GB`; the flag wins when both are given. Separate from the resident ceiling on purpose: a chat model must not be able to crowd out the diffusion worker, and a video pipeline must not evict the model currently answering requests. On a memory-constrained box, the 60/40 default split can leave this tier too small for a single on-demand pipeline — raise it explicitly when that happens. |
| `--tier` | `TIER` | `TENZRO_TIER` |  | Resource tier: `auto` (default), `edge`, `validator` or `provider`. Sets the defaults for the store's memory and background work and the runtime's threads; `auto` picks `provider` for roles that run models, `edge` on a machine with at most 8 GiB of memory, `validator` otherwise. Values set under `[storage]` win over the tier. |
| `--worker-threads` | `N` | `TENZRO_WORKER_THREADS` |  | Async runtime worker threads. Omit for the tier's: 2, or 1 on a one-core edge device. |
| `--roles` / `-r` | `ROLES` |  |  | Node roles, comma-separated (e.g. "validator,storage,ai"). A node may serve any combination of roles under a single stake. Aliases accepted: validator, model-provider/ai, tee-provider/tee, storage, edge/ingress, user/light. |
| `--validator-self-stake` | `WEI` |  |  | Self-stake in wei to auto-register this node as a validator on boot (permissionless / first-boot onboarding). Requires the validator role; the node's validator-derived account must hold this stake plus gas. Omit to disable self-registration. |
| `--consensus-key-scheme` | `SCHEME` |  |  | Signature scheme of this node's consensus key: COMPSIG-MLDSA65-ECDSA-P256 (the default) or COMPSIG-MLDSA87-ECDSA-P384, which needs a TPM implementing ML-DSA and P-384. A validator registered under another scheme rotates to the key of this one. |
| `--boot-nodes` / `-b` | `IDENTITIES` |  |  | Boot identities (comma-separated): machine identities, each optionally with the relay it is reachable through, `did:tenzro:machine:<id>[@<relay url>]`. Network addresses are refused. Also read, and appended, from `TENZRO_BOOT_NODES`. Omitting this joins the public network through its genesis validators' identities. Pass an explicitly empty value — `--boot-nodes ""` — to stay **isolated**: no dialling out. That is what a local or solo node wants, and it is distinct from omitting the flag. |
| `--relay-listen` | `ADDR` |  |  | Serve the relay role: the address the relay's HTTP listener binds. Requires `--relay-url`. |
| `--relay-url` | `URL` |  |  | The URL peers reach this node's relay at, announced in its signed endpoint record. Exposing the listener at that URL, with TLS, is the operator's choice outside the node. |
| `--relay-udp-port` | `PORT` |  |  | UDP port this node's endpoint binds while it serves the relay role (default 443). Only for a host that runs several relays, such as a test cluster; one process per host can hold a port. |
| `--log-level` | `LEVEL` |  | `info` | Log level (trace, debug, info, warn, error) |
| `--log-format` | `FORMAT` |  | `text` | Log format: "text" for human-readable, "json" for structured JSON |
| `--rpc-addr` | `ADDR` |  |  | RPC listen address. Loopback only (default `127.0.0.1:8545`): the node never exposes its machine. To serve RPC publicly, put your own reverse proxy in front of this address and pass its URL as `--external-rpc-addr`. |
| `--web-addr` | `ADDR` |  |  | Web API listen address. Loopback only (default `127.0.0.1:8080`). |
| `--genesis` / `-g` | `FILE` |  |  | Path to genesis configuration file |
| `--solo` |  |  |  | Run a self-contained solo chain: fabricate a single-validator genesis with this node as the only validator, and let it form quorum alone. This is for local development and isolated/sovereign bring-up ONLY. A validator meant to join the public network must NEVER run solo — doing so silently forks a private chain that only cosmetically resembles the real network (same chain_id), peers with it, and then diverges at QC verification. Requiring an explicit opt-in is what keeps "join the network" from degrading into "fork my own chain" when a genesis file is missing. Implied automatically by isolated mode (`--boot-nodes ""`). Rejected if combined with a real `--genesis` file or with configured boot peers. |
| `--dev` |  |  |  | Run a local developer chain: a solo chain that dials no one, with one-minute epochs and quarter-second rounds, and the `--fund` accounts funded at genesis. Its validator and identity keys are this machine's TPM or Secure Enclave keys; a machine with neither is refused. Started by `tenzro dev`. |
| `--fund` | `ADDRESS` |  |  | An account funded with 1,000,000 TNZO at a developer chain's genesis, 32-byte hex. Repeatable. Only with `--dev`. |
| `--mcp-addr` | `ADDR` |  |  | MCP server listen address. Loopback only (default `127.0.0.1:3001`). |
| `--a2a-addr` | `ADDR` |  |  | A2A protocol server listen address. Loopback only (default `127.0.0.1:3002`). |
| `--external-rpc-addr` | `URL` |  |  | Public https URL of your own edge (reverse proxy) in front of this node's loopback RPC listener, if you expose it. The only RPC URL the node publishes; without it none is published. Refused at startup when it is not https or names a loopback, private, CGNAT or link-local host. |
| `--external-mcp-addr` | `URL` |  |  | Public https URL of your own edge in front of this node's loopback MCP listener, if you expose it. Same rules as `--external-rpc-addr`. |
| `--state-sync-from` | `ENDPOINT_ID[@IP:PORT]` |  |  | State sync: restore the committed state from these peers (their current iroh `EndpointId`s, as their signed announcements give them; repeat the flag for several) before starting consensus, instead of replaying blocks. `<EndpointId>@<ip:port>` dials that address directly, for a network with no discovery (repeat it to give several addresses of one peer); a bare id is found by discovery. Also settable as `state_sync_from` in the config file. The snapshot is fetched as BLAKE3-verified blobs from any peer that has them and checked bucket by bucket against the state root that the `--checkpoint-hash` block commits. The recovery after a corrupt store (`scripts/repair-validator-store.sh`, then restart with this flag) works on a fixed `bind_addr` too: the state-sync endpoint is released before the node's own endpoint binds. Requires `--checkpoint-height` and `--checkpoint-hash`. |
| `--checkpoint-hash` | `HEX` |  |  | Weak-subjectivity checkpoint: the hash (hex, with or without `0x`) of a finalized block the operator has verified out of band, at `--checkpoint-height`. Every import path refuses any other block at that height, which defeats a long-range fork that passes certificate verification, and state sync restores the state this block commits. |
| `--checkpoint-height` | `HEIGHT` |  |  | Height of the `--checkpoint-hash` block. |
| `--recovery-manifest` | `FILE` |  |  | Recovery restart after a halt below quorum: the manifest file (JSON) that the surviving operators and the successor validators agreed on. Applied once at start, before consensus is seated, and only at the manifest's anchor block, so it does nothing on a chain that has moved on. Needs `--recovery-digest` and the anchor as `--checkpoint-height` and `--checkpoint-hash`. See docs/RECOVERY-BELOW-QUORUM.md. |
| `--recovery-digest` | `HEX` |  |  | The manifest digest (hex) the operator compared with the one published on independent channels. The node refuses to start if the file's digest differs. |
| `--recovery-confirm` | `HEX` |  |  | The recovery root (hex) every member printed with `--recovery-check`. The node starts only if its own root equals it. |
| `--recovery-check` |  |  |  | Run every recovery check, print the recovery root and exit without changing anything, so the members can compare roots before applying. |
| `--accept-non-commercial` |  |  | `false` | Admit NonCommercial-tier models. Off by default: a node refuses to load any model whose license forbids commercial use unless the operator opts in with this flag. Serving inference is a commercial act on a paid network, so the default is fail-closed. |
| `--accept-license` | `ID` |  |  | Admit a CommercialCustom-tier model family by its license id (repeatable / comma-separated), e.g. `--accept-license gemma --accept-license dinov3`. Custom-license families (Gemma Terms, DINOv3, Meta SAM) require the operator to have read and accepted the upstream terms; the node refuses to load them until their id appears here. |
| `--catalog-publisher` | `DID` |  |  | DID of a publisher this node serves catalog models from; repeat or comma-separate for several. Without any, every bonded publisher. |
| `--release-publisher` | `DID` |  |  | DID of a publisher whose engine releases this node reports as available; repeat or comma-separate for several. |
| `--kyc-asset` | `TOKEN_ID` |  |  | Token id (hex) of an asset whose policy names the KYC issuers this node recognises; repeat or comma-separate for several. Without any, every identity's KYC tier is unverified. |
| `--territory-mode` | `MODE` |  | `enforce` | How to handle models whose licence restricts the territories they may be served to. Most licences carry no such term — seven of the eight custom licences in the catalog are unrestricted — so this affects only the few that do, and costs nothing for everything else. * `enforce` (default) — check the caller's territory per request. Requires `--territory-db`. * `refuse-restricted` — do not serve territorially-restricted models at all. Needs no database: it removes the obligation rather than the enforcement of it, and is the right setting for an operator who does not want these models. |
| `--territory-db` | `PATH` |  |  | Path to an mmdb country database for territorial enforcement. Use a database you may redistribute: DB-IP Lite Country (CC BY 4.0) or sapics/ip-location-db `user-country` (PDDL-1.0, public domain). MaxMind GeoLite2 is **not** suitable — its EULA requires deleting superseded databases within 30 days of a release, which a distributed binary cannot honour, and redistribution needs a paid licence. Without one, `enforce` refuses territorially-restricted models — and only those. Every other model keeps serving. |
| `--territory-db-label` | `LABEL` |  |  | A label for the territory database, recorded on every decision (e.g. `dbip-country-lite-2026-08`). A decision has to stay interpretable after the database is updated underneath it: both a bloc's membership and an address's allocation can change, so "which data said so" is part of the record. |
| `--trusted-proxy` | `IP` |  |  | Reverse proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` this node will believe. Without this, the header is ignored entirely and the socket address is used — which is correct: any client can set `X-Forwarded-For`, so trusting it unconditionally turns the whole check into a no-op. |
| `--local-territory` | `CC` |  |  | Territory to record for callers on this machine or its private network (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. `SG`). Local addresses cannot be geolocated. Absent this, they are treated like any other unresolvable caller and refused for restricted models. Setting it is an operator attestation about their own deployment, and is recorded as such rather than as a measurement. |
| `<COMMAND>` | `Option<Command>` |  |  |  |

## Subcommands

### `tenzro-node init`

Print this machine's validator public keys (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) for genesis assembly. Nothing is generated or written: the keys are derived on demand from this machine's TPM or Secure Enclave, and the same machine always derives the same keys. Refuses on a machine with neither.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | The node's data directory. Also settable via `$TENZRO_DATA_DIR`. |
| `--stake` | `u64` |  | `1_000_000` | Genesis stake to print in the emitted `[[validators]]` stanza. Does not write anything on-chain — this is purely a convenience for the operator assembling genesis.toml. |
| `--format` | `FORMAT` |  | `toml` | Output format. `toml` (default) emits a ready-to-paste `[[validators]]` stanza; `json` the same entry as an object. |

### `tenzro-node validator-entry`

Print this machine's `[[validators]]` genesis entry, signed by its hardware consensus key. Refuses on a machine without one.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | Data directory holding the node key. |
| `--stake` | `u64` |  |  | Stake for the entry, in whole TNZO. |
| `--relay-url` | `URL` |  |  | URL of the relay this validator is reachable through (its own relay role's URL, or a relay it uses), so nodes can join through its identity. |

### `tenzro-node graceful-exit`

Ask the running node to step down gracefully. Calls `tenzro_gracefulExit` on the local RPC. The node waits until it leads none of the next consensus rounds its schedule looks ahead over, then triggers its existing shutdown path (the in-process `NodeEvent::Shutdown` plus the 5-second drain in `main()`). Intended for K8s `preStop` hooks and systemd `ExecStop=` units — a 0 exit means the node accepted the request, not that the process has already died. Wait on the process or the pod terminationGracePeriodSeconds for the actual exit.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--rpc-url` | `URL` |  | `http://127.0.0.1:8545` | JSON-RPC endpoint of the running node. |
| `--max-wait-secs` | `u64` |  | `60` | Cap on how long to wait for leader rotation. Defaults to 60s, far longer than the rounds the schedule looks ahead over take even when leaders time out. |
| `--force` |  |  | `false` | Skip the leader-clearance check entirely and trigger shutdown immediately. Use only when you know the node is not currently producing or about to produce a block. |

### `tenzro-node backup`

Copy the node's newest epoch snapshot to DEST. Only SST files no earlier backup under DEST holds are copied; the rest are hardlinked from there, so every backup directory is a complete store. Runs at idle priority, paced to --rate-mb. The node never sends a backup anywhere itself: schedule this, and encrypt or ship DEST, however you choose. Safe while the node runs.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | The node's data directory. |
| `--dest` | `DEST` |  |  | Destination directory for backups. |
| `--rate-mb` | `u64` |  | `64` | Copy rate, MiB per second (0 for unpaced). |

### `tenzro-node access`

Set who may use this node: the access wizard. Writes `access.toml` in the data directory through the same store the running node and its admin page use: validated, versioned, logged, applied by a running node within seconds. With no options it asks.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | The node's data directory. |
| `--preset` | `Option<String>` |  |  | Rule for every surface and class no other rule covers: open, closed, signed_in or agents_with_terms. |
| `--admin` | `DID` |  |  | Add a DID that may administer this node besides its operator. |
| `--remove-admin` | `DID` |  |  | Remove an administrator DID. |
| `--token-ttl-secs` | `Option<u64>` |  |  | Lifetime of issued access tokens, in seconds. |
| `--show` |  |  |  | Print the policy in force and change nothing. |
| `--page` |  |  |  | Open the admin page: write a fifteen-minute ticket and print the page's address on this node's RPC listener. |
| `--rpc-url` | `String` |  | `http://127.0.0.1:8545` | This node's RPC listener, for --page. |

### `tenzro-node restore`

Rebuild the node's store from an epoch snapshot or backup. The snapshot's checkpoint must be certified: a proof from genesis (the proof kept with the snapshot, one fetched from --proof-from, or one given with --proof) must verify every certificate's quorum signatures against the committee of its epoch, starting from the genesis committee, and the snapshot's state must rebuild the certified state root; otherwise nothing is restored. The node must be stopped and its store directory absent or empty.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | `TENZRO_DATA_DIR` |  | The node's data directory. |
| `--snapshot` | `DIR` |  |  | The snapshot or backup directory to restore from. |
| `--chain-id` | `u64` |  |  | Chain id, from the genesis file. |
| `--genesis-hash` | `HEX` |  |  | Genesis block hash (hex), from the genesis file. |
| `--genesis-committee-root` | `HEX` |  |  | Root of the genesis committee (hex), from the genesis file. |
| `--proof-from` | `URL` |  |  | Fetch the checkpoint proof from this peer's RPC endpoint. |
| `--proof` | `FILE` |  |  | Read the checkpoint proof (bincode) from this file. |
| `--handover-program` | `HEX` |  |  | Image id (hex) of the handover program, from the chain's governance: needed when the proof builds on a handover chain proof rather than on every handover from genesis. |

### `tenzro-node prover-inputs`

Write what a prover needs to extend the handover chain proof, as `tenzro-finality-prover handover` reads it: the node's newest chain proof receipt (`prev.bin`), the genesis committee root (`genesis-root`) and, per epoch since, the handover and the members of that epoch's committee (`<epoch>/handover.bin`, `<epoch>/members.bin`).

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--rpc-url` | `URL` |  | `http://127.0.0.1:8545` | The node's RPC endpoint. |
| `--out` | `DIR` |  |  | The directory to write into. |

### `tenzro-node credentials`

This operator's own credentials: for model origins, and for the endpoint a connector forwards to. Optional: a node without one serves every open model and fetches gated weights from network peers. Run it on the node's own machine; the credential is sealed to this machine's TPM or Secure Enclave and never leaves it.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<ACTION>` | `CredentialsAction` |  |  |  |

### `tenzro-node tpm`

This machine's TPM. The node account key is a P-256 key held in the TPM or Secure Enclave plus an ML-DSA-65 key: inside a TPM implementing library v1.85, otherwise derived on demand from the machine's hardware-held derivation root and never stored. The account's first transaction enrols the ML-DSA-65 key on chain.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<ACTION>` | `TpmAction` |  |  |  |

### `tenzro-node hardware`

Report what this binary was built for and whether it can use this machine's accelerators, then exit: the same check the node runs at startup, without starting a node. Exits non-zero when the node would refuse to start here.

### `tenzro-node doctor`

Report whether peers can reach this node, and how to fix it when they cannot: IPv4 and IPv6, the router's port mapping (UPnP, PCP, NAT-PMP), the host firewall, and, from the running node, the NAT in front of it, the addresses peers see it at and the relay it uses. Run it on the node's own machine.

| Flag | Value | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  |  |  | Print the report as JSON. |
| `--allow-inbound` |  |  |  | Also let peers reach this node directly through the host firewall, with a rule scoped to this binary and its UDP port: on Windows an inbound rule for the private and public profiles (and removal of block rules a dismissed prompt left for this binary), on macOS an entry in the application firewall. Optional: the node works without it, through relays and hole punching. Needs an administrator PowerShell on Windows and sudo on macOS. On Linux it prints the command for your firewall. |


## Node tiers

Tenzro runs on every class of machine, from small embedded and edge devices
to the largest GPU servers, from one codebase. The network's tiers are edge
(light) nodes on small machines, which run agents today and are designed to
host orchestration; standard nodes on CPU servers; GPU providers; and
validators. They are built from the release
variants below: the light build serves edge nodes and validators, the
standard build serves CPU servers, and the standard build with a GPU backend
serves GPU providers.

One `tenzro-node` source builds for three tiers. A tier is a build (which
cargo features are compiled in) and a resource preset (what the node takes of
the machine at run time). The build decides which roles a node can fill; the
preset only sizes it.

| Tier | Machines | Build | Roles it refuses |
|---|---|---|---|
| edge | Small, embedded and edge devices: single-board computers (the Raspberry Pi is the reference device), Jetson-class modules, mini PCs, NAS boxes, gateways | `scripts/build-tier.sh edge` (light build, `edge` profile) | `ai`, `compute`, `tee` |
| validator | Servers that validate, store and relay | `scripts/build-tier.sh validator` (light build, release profile) | `ai`, `compute`, `tee` |
| provider | Servers that also serve models | `scripts/build-tier.sh provider [cuda\|rocm\|vulkan\|metal\|...]` (standard build plus a GPU backend) | none; a GPU build with no usable GPU refuses to start |

### Light build for small machines

The standard build compiles the model engines in: llama.cpp/ggml, media
generation, LoRA training, the ONNX runtimes and their decoders and
tokenizers. They come with the `inference` cargo feature of `tenzro-node`,
which is on by default and turns on the `engine` feature of `tenzro-model`.
Every fleet and test script builds with it, unchanged.

The light build leaves it out:

```
cargo build --release -p tenzro-node --no-default-features
```

It keeps identity (including the remote-TPM client for a machine with no TPM
of its own), payments, the agent surfaces, RPC, MCP and A2A, consensus,
storage, block sync and the `light`, `micro`, `fullnode`, `rpc`, `storage` and
`validator` roles. A chat, completion, embedding, rerank, segmentation,
detection, forecast, transcription, speech or media-render call for a model a
provider on the network serves is forwarded to that provider as the standard
build forwards it. What would run a model on the node itself is refused with
error -32004 naming the light build: loading and unloading models, training,
MoE expert hosting, the layer pipeline, realtime speech turns, and a modality
call no provider offers.

Started with `ai`, `compute` or `tee` (on the command line or in the
configuration file), the light build exits before it opens any key or file:

```
this tenzro-node is the light build (built without the `inference` feature) and cannot serve the ai role: it runs models on this machine. ...
```

### Resource presets

`--tier` (`TENZRO_TIER`, or `tier = "..."` in the configuration file) takes
`auto` (the default), `edge`, `validator` or `provider`. `auto` picks
`provider` for roles that run models, `edge` on a machine with at most 8 GiB
of memory (`[memory] total_gb` when set, else detected), and `validator`
otherwise.

| Setting | edge | validator, provider | Override |
|---|---|---|---|
| Store memory (block cache with the memtables charged to it) | 1/16 of the memory pool, 32 MiB to 256 MiB | 1/32 of the pool, 256 MiB to 4 GiB | `[storage] memory_mb` |
| Write buffer per column family | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | `[storage] write_buffer_mb` |
| Background flush and compaction jobs | 1 | 2 | `[storage] background_jobs` |
| Background write rate | 16 MiB/s | 64 MiB/s | `[storage] background_write_mb_per_sec` |
| Open files | 256 | 1000 | `[storage] max_open_files` |
| Runtime worker threads | 2 (1 on a one-core machine) | 2 | `--worker-threads` / `TENZRO_WORKER_THREADS` |
| Runtime blocking threads | 32 | 512 | |

The memory pool is what the node's memory budget lends out: on a machine with
less than twice the 16 GiB default reserve, three quarters of it. So the edge
store takes 96 MiB on a 2 GB board, 192 MiB on 4 GB and 256 MiB from 8 GB up.
The validator and provider presets are the defaults every node had before the
tiers.

History retention is a network parameter (governance), not a preset: every
non-archival node keeps the governed window, prunes to it and compacts when
the data volume passes `[storage] prune_watermark_pct` (75%), and refuses
non-essential data past `refuse_watermark_pct` (90%). On a small SD card or
eMMC those watermarks are what keep the node inside its disk.

The background tasks a node starts are already gated by role: audit
watchers, fee-rate reporting, SLA probes and attestations, data-availability
retention and the optimistic reviewer return at once on a node whose roles do
not use them. The light build additionally starts none of the model runtimes,
the standby loop, the residency schedule, the autotune sampler,
session continuity or the MoE repair loop.

### Raspberry Pi and other edge devices

- **Processor.** `scripts/build-tier.sh edge` builds for any aarch64 (or
  x86_64) machine. `--cpu cortex-a76` tunes it for a Pi 5; the result uses
  instructions a Pi 4 (Cortex-A72) does not have and does not run there.
  `--cpu cortex-a72` builds for a Pi 4. `--size` optimises for size.
- **C library.** A binary built on Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) needs glibc
  2.38 or later: it runs on Raspberry Pi OS based on Debian 13 (glibc 2.41),
  not on Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm (glibc 2.36). For Bookworm, build on
  Bookworm or with a toolchain pinned to glibc 2.36.
- **Page size.** The Pi 5 kernel uses 16K pages by default. The node uses the
  system allocator, and nothing in its dependencies assumes 4K pages.
- **Identity.** A Pi has no TPM. It keeps its identity key in another
  machine's TPM through `tenzro-node tpm serve` on that machine. The provider
  listens on loopback only unless its file names the addresses to serve on,
  such as `listen = ["100.64.0.7:7400"]` for its private-network (VPN) address. On the Pi,
  `tenzro-node tpm key-holder` runs as its own service: it makes this boot's
  transport key in memory (never on disk) and the operator approves it with
  a passkey grant (`tpm grant-request`, then `tpm grant-install`); the node
  starts with `--tpm-key-holder <socket> --tpm-label <label>`. The node can
  restart without a new grant; a reboot needs one.

  **Validators.** The same delegation can hold a validator's consensus key.
  The P-256 leg is a key in the provider's TPM and the ML-DSA-65 leg is
  derived there for each use, so a machine with no TPM of its own can take
  the validator role. The provider file must enrol the client with
  `derived = true`. The limits: every signature is a round trip to the
  provider, queued behind its other TPM commands, so the provider must stay
  reachable; a grant lasts at most the provider's `max_grant_hours` (720 by
  default), and after a reboot of the key holder, or when the grant ends,
  the validator cannot sign until the operator installs a new one. The
  ML-DSA-87 / P-384 consensus scheme is not available this way: it needs a
  TPM in the validator's own machine that implements ML-DSA and P-384. A
  passkey never holds a consensus key: the operator's passkey grants and
  approves, and the key stays in a TPM or Secure Enclave.

  **Session delegation.** A TPM command takes seconds, so the key holder does
  not ask the provider for every signature. With `tenzro-node tpm key-holder
  --identity <did> --label <label>` it asks the provider once per session for
  a delegation: a statement signed by the identity key (its Ed25519 and its
  ML-DSA-65 leg) that binds a session key pair the holder made in its own
  locked memory, for a bounded time and under the identity's current key
  version. The holder then signs each message with the session key
  (`OP_SESSION_SIGN`, no round trip), and a peer traces the signature to the
  identity key through the delegation. The session key is made at start,
  wiped on drop, never written and never exported; it is a credential for
  one delegation, not an identity key. The delegation ends at its expiry, at
  its revocation, at the end of the grant it was issued under, or when the
  identity rotates to a new key version, whichever comes first. The holder
  renews before expiry (`--session-renew-before-secs`), checks the provider
  for revocation and rotation every `--session-check-secs`, and a provider
  that cannot be reached changes nothing until the delegation expires, after
  which signing fails closed. A cold start with the provider down is refused.
  After a reboot the holder has a new transport key; the operator makes one
  new passkey grant (`tpm grant-request`, `tpm grant-install`) and the
  session starts from it with nothing else to do. The grant and the session
  key are kept in memory only. `tpm session-status` prints the delegation's
  end and id; `tpm revoke --config <provider file> --delegation <id>`
  revokes one.

  The provider issues delegations when its file names an `issuer_file`, a
  JSON file the identity's on-chain key update rewrites:
  `{"identities": {"<did>": {"version": 2, "label": "<key label>"}}}`. The
  provider derives the identity key under that label in its TPM; no handle or
  key id is configured anywhere. The limits are provider-file values, not
  constants: `delegation_max_lifetime_secs`, `delegation_min_lifetime_secs`,
  `revocation_file`, and for the TPM command queue `tpm_queue_max_waiting`,
  `tpm_queue_max_wait_secs`, `tpm_retries`, `tpm_backoff_base_ms`,
  `tpm_backoff_cap_ms`. The provider runs one TPM command at a time; a
  request that finds the line full, or that waits its limit, is refused with
  `tpm busy: ... retry in N ms`, and the key holder waits that long and asks
  again (`--busy-retries`, `--request-timeout-secs`).
- **Memory.** The light node's resident memory measured 130 to 210 MiB idle
  and up to about 230 MiB under RPC load (below), within a 2 GB board's
  budget beside the operating system (about 200 to 250 MiB idle on Raspberry
  Pi OS Lite 64-bit).
- **Storage.** Use an SSD or NVMe where the board takes one: the store's
  compaction is paced, but an SD card's random-write rate is low.

Not built yet: 32-bit ARM (armv7) and RISC-V (riscv64). Their dependency
trees resolve; what has not been checked by a build is RocksDB on a 32-bit
target, the native code in aws-lc-sys, ring and blst on them, and the zero-
knowledge verifiers (risc0, plonky3, halo2) on 32-bit.

### Measurements

Measured on an aarch64 host (20 cores, Ubuntu 24.04) on 2026-10-18, against a
private network of three nodes on software TPMs (one validator, one full node
serving the relay, and the node under test with `--roles light` and
`[memory] total_gb` set to emulate a smaller machine). The node under test
started from an empty data directory; sync time is from process start to the
validator's height at that moment. Idle and loaded samples are 60 s each;
the load is 40 JSON-RPC reads per second. The host was running other builds,
so CPU and sync figures carry noise of tens of percent.

Run A had a dev calendar (an epoch every few seconds, with an epoch snapshot
each); run B the default calendar (day-long epochs). Both produce about one
block a second. RSS is resident memory, mean / maximum over the sample.

| Build | Binary (stripped) | Emulated memory | Store | Sync | Idle RSS | Idle CPU | Loaded RSS | Loaded CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard (all engines), A | 132.4 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 7.7 blocks/s | 232 / 262 MiB | 57% | 262 / 268 MiB | 97% |
| Standard (all engines), B | 132.4 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 5.4 blocks/s | 157 / 172 MiB | 77% | 173 / 177 MiB | 97% |
| Light, before the presets, A | 86.8 MB | 4 GB | 256 MiB, 2 jobs | 9.2 blocks/s | 173 / 183 MiB | 89% | 185 / 188 MiB | 83% |
| Light, before the presets, B | 86.8 MB | 4 GB | 256 MiB, 2 jobs | 7.1 blocks/s | 144 / 167 MiB | 70% | 166 / 169 MiB | 96% |
| Light, edge preset, A | 86.8 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 6.1 blocks/s | 153 / 189 MiB | 51% | 190 / 193 MiB | 104% |
| Light, edge preset, B | 86.8 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 6.7 blocks/s | 140 / 151 MiB | 99% | 152 / 157 MiB | 96% |
| Light, edge preset, A | 86.8 MB | 2 GB | 96 MiB, 1 job | 6.8 blocks/s | 173 / 210 MiB | 40% | 204 / 209 MiB | 101% |
| Light, edge preset, B | 86.8 MB | 2 GB | 96 MiB, 1 job | 7.5 blocks/s | 154 / 171 MiB | 71% | 170 / 174 MiB | 94% |
| Light, validator preset, A | 86.8 MB | 16 GB | 384 MiB, 2 jobs | 7.5 blocks/s | 199 / 220 MiB | 86% | 222 / 225 MiB | 97% |
| Edge profile, `--cpu cortex-a76`, A | 85.5 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 8.5 blocks/s | 181 / 218 MiB | 41% | 218 / 222 MiB | 107% |
| Edge profile, `--size`, A | 62.2 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 7.6 blocks/s | 180 / 190 MiB | 24% | 215 / 229 MiB | 94% |
| Edge profile, `--size`, B | 62.2 MB | 4 GB | 192 MiB, 1 job | 5.4 blocks/s | 132 / 168 MiB | 46% | 166 / 172 MiB | 88% |

What the numbers show:

- The light build is 35% smaller than the standard build (86.8 MB against
  132.4 MB stripped; the standard test-build binary with line tables is
  979 MB) and holds 15 to 80 MiB less resident memory in the same role.
- In a sync this short the store's cache never fills, so the presets change
  resident memory less than the noise; what they bound is the ceiling the
  store can grow to over a long run (96 MiB on a 2 GB board instead of 256).
- `--size` saves another 28% of the binary with no loss in sync or RPC load
  that this host can resolve.
- A light node following a chain that makes a block a second keeps about one
  core busy on that host. That is block import, not idle overhead, and is the
  figure to watch on a Pi 4.

On the same network the validator (light build, validator role) held
237 MiB on average with peaks of 614 MiB at epoch boundaries and 38% of a
core; the full node serving the relay held 365 MiB and 85% of a core.

Check a build against its budget with `scripts/edge-budget.sh <binary>
[<measurement>]` (the release gate runs it as row L4): 100 MB stripped, and
256 MiB idle and 320 MiB loaded resident memory for a `--roles light` node.
